title: MRI OF THE LUMBOSACRAL SPINE (PLAIN)
author: Dr. Kamrul Hasan, MBBS, MD (Radiology)
impression:
1. L4-L5: broad-based disc bulge with a superimposed right paracentral disc protrusion causing moderate right lateral recess narrowing and contact with the traversing right L5 nerve root. Mild bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.
2. L5-S1: mild disc desiccation and bulge without nerve root compression.
3. Multilevel facet arthropathy, worst at L4-L5. No spinal canal stenosis of significance at other levels.
4. No fracture, marrow lesion or paraspinal collection.

diagnoses.text: L4-L5 right paracentral disc protrusion contacting the right L5 nerve root

follow_ups.text: Consider spine or neurosurgical opinion if the radicular symptoms persist despite conservative management.

notes: Date printed day first (08/10/2026 read as 8 October 2026).

sections.heading: Clinical information
sections.text: Low back pain for 6 weeks radiating to the right leg with tingling over the dorsum of the right foot. No bladder or bowel symptoms.

sections.heading: Technique
sections.text: Multiplanar, multi-echo MRI of the lumbosacral spine was performed with sagittal T1W, T2W and STIR and axial T2W images through L1 to S1. No contrast was given.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text:
Alignment: Normal lumbar lordosis is preserved. No spondylolisthesis.
Vertebral bodies: Normal height and marrow signal. Small Schmorl's node at the superior endplate of L3. No fracture or focal marrow lesion.
Conus medullaris: Ends at the L1 level and shows normal signal.
L1-L2, L2-L3 and L3-L4: Discs are normal in height and signal. No significant canal or foraminal narrowing.
L4-L5: Disc desiccation with a broad-based posterior bulge and a superimposed right paracentral protrusion indenting the thecal sac. This narrows the right lateral recess moderately and contacts the traversing right L5 nerve root. Mild bilateral neural foraminal narrowing; the exiting L4 roots are free. Facet joint hypertrophy and ligamentum flavum thickening are noted. AP canal diameter 10 mm.
L5-S1: Mild disc desiccation and a small diffuse bulge without nerve root compression. Neural foramina are patent.
Paraspinal soft tissues: Normal. No collection.
Sacroiliac joints (partially seen): Unremarkable.

sections.heading: Impression
sections.text:
1. L4-L5: broad-based disc bulge with a superimposed right paracentral disc protrusion causing moderate right lateral recess narrowing and contact with the traversing right L5 nerve root. Mild bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.
2. L5-S1: mild disc desiccation and bulge without nerve root compression.
3. Multilevel facet arthropathy, worst at L4-L5. No spinal canal stenosis of significance at other levels.
4. No fracture, marrow lesion or paraspinal collection.

sections.heading: Advice
sections.text: Clinical and neurological correlation is suggested. Consider spine or neurosurgical opinion if the radicular symptoms persist despite conservative management.
